content:
amanda: Heads-up — security review found a partner S3 bucket with a ZIP that included our service's KMS ciphertext blobs and a legacy service token. Bucket was public for ~48h.
ben: ack. is the ciphertext raw KMS blob or wrapped in partner tooling?
amanda: raw ciphertexts (AWS KMS). partner config included `leaked_creds.zip` with several files: `token.txt`, `keys/enc_blob.bin`.
josh: ugly. token is long-lived? any evidence of it being used?
amanda: token is scoped to staging but had broader service-account role attached historically. CloudTrail shows one unusual GET from an IP we don't recognize ~36h ago.
maria: Can we rotate/rewrap without breaking partner integration? need safe path.
amanda: Proposed immediate steps: 1) contain access to bucket (partner already made it private) 2) rotate the long-lived token (revoke + issue ephemeral) 3) rewrap KMS ciphertext to new CMK with strict IAM conditions 4) tighten decrypt RBAC and enable replays in audit logs.
ops-oncall: I locked the partner bucket and added an object lock lifecycle to stop accidental public ACLs. also kicked a rotate of the staging token.
sec-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-7432 — severity: medium. Assigned: eng-security, infra-oncall.
ben: For rewrap: we can use AWS KMS ReEncrypt to move ciphertext to a new key id. command for reference:
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_blob.bin \
  --source-region us-east-1 \
  --destination-key-id alias/redwood-rotated-key \
  --output text > rewrapped_blob.bin
```
ben: But re-encrypt only helps if the original key remains usable. if key grants decrypt to broad principals we need to revoke those first.
josh: Suggest flow: A) revoke decrypt on old CMK for partner SA B) re-encrypt copies (so partner can pull rewrapped) C) rotate partner integration to use new alias D) expire old ciphertexts & audit.
maria: How do we let partner migrate? they pull blobs and decrypt with our key. If we revoke decrypt first they'll be blocked. we should coordinate a handoff window.
amanda: propose phased window: 1h notice + 15m canary for a single partner blob, then full swap. schedule in next 30m? partner ready?
ops-oncall: Partner rep confirmed availability at +45m. canary ok.
ben: RBAC changes: create a short-lived role `kms/ephemeral-decrypt` with condition on invoker: `aws:SourceIp` OR workload identity. grant Decrypt only and limited to 30m sessions. update key policy to allow sts:AssumeRole by that role.
josh: Also enable CloudTrail insights/audit for ReEncrypt and Decrypt on that CMK. we need immutable logs for any rewraps.
maria: Vault idea: create Vault-wrapped ephemeral keys so partner never holds long-lived tokens. flow: partner authenticates to Vault (OIDC) -> Vault issues 1h data key (transit) which is used to decrypt payload, then Vault records audit. worth adding as longer-term fix.
amanda: Agreed — medium-term: migrate partner to Vault transit or KMS via ephemeralization. Short-term we need clear runbook.
ben: Draft runbook (short form):
- T+0: Make bucket private (done)
- T+5: Revoke staging token and create immediate ephemeral replacement (ops)
- T+15: Modify CMK policy to remove partner SA decrypt (temp deny)
- T+20: Re-encrypt critical blobs to `alias/redwood-rotated-key` and place in partner's private bucket path `rotated/`
- T+30: Partner performs canary decrypt and reports success
- T+45: Full rollout and rotate integration config to new alias
- T+60: Retire old ciphertexts and re-enable tighter key policy (deny by default)
- Post: 1) run a permissions audit 2) create Vault ephemeral rollout ticket
amanda: assigning tasks: ops-oncall -> revoke token & create ephemeral; ben -> CMK policy change + re-encrypt; josh -> enable audit trails + CloudTrail export; maria -> partner comms and canary coordination.
ops-oncall: started token revoke now, ETA 5m.
sec-bot: Key actions recorded in incident timeline.
maria: partner confirms canary at +45m, will standby in slack.
ben: one important note: when we re-encrypt we must preserve ciphertext integrity for any tooling that expects a specific envelope format. test on canary blob first.
josh: testing on canary now — decrypt of rewrapped blob via `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://rewrapped_blob.bin --key-id alias/redwood-rotated-key` returns expected plaintext.
amanda: Nice. also enabling per-request token binding in our client SDK so future tokens are non-replayable.
ben: after rollback window closes, we will add a KMS condition on encrypt/decrypt that requires `aws:PrincipalTag/role=partner` and `aws:RequestTag/usage=ephemeral` for partner decrypts. that'll block leaked blobs used outside expected context.
maria: I'll draft a short partner postmortem and checklist: disclosure, what was exposed, timeline, steps we took, and recommendations (ephemeral keys, Vault transit, stricter ACLs).
ops-oncall: token revoke done. partner confirmed they can't use old token anymore.
sec-bot: Update: incident severity downgraded to low after revoke + canary success.
amanda: Follow-ups: create ticket to rotate all staging long-lived tokens, add automated S3 public ACL monitor alert, and schedule Vault transit migration epic.
ben: I'll open the CMK policy PR and include the IAM condition snippet.
josh: I'll export CloudTrail logs to our secure bucket and attach to incident.
maria: thanks everyone. closing loop after postmortem doc in 24h. :+1:
ops-oncall: ack, will follow up if anything odd shows in audit.
sec-bot: Incident #INC-2026-7432 closed (monitoring).
